items.title: Constructing restructured jujube using blackened jujube pulp and carrageenan to resolve Peel-induced rough mouthfeel.
items.authors: Zhang H, Wang Y, Sun X, Gao L, Zhang D, Zhang R.
items.abstract: Blackened jujube offers improved nutritional value, while its peel-induced coarse mouthfeel limits its broader use in snack-style products. To address this limitation, this study proposes restructuring blackened jujube pulp into self-supporting composite gels using κ-carrageenan (KC). While neither 0.5% KC nor the pulp alone formed a self-supporting gel, composite gels containing 0.5% KC were observed to be self-supporting, indicating that the pulp matrix facilitates gelation at a lower KC level. Increasing KC from 0.5% to 2.5% progressively strengthened the network, increasing hardness from ~2.5 N to 16.7 N, water-holding capacity from 53.45% to 77.01%, and freeze-thaw syneresis from 68.94% to 26.69%, alongside network densification and T₂₂ shortening (75.8 to 37.0 ms). Sensory evaluation also confirmed that restructuring markedly reduced grittiness and improved overall mouthfeel. Overall, this work offers a practical strategy for converting fruit pulps into self-supporting composite gels, thereby enabling blackened jujube products with tunable texture and improved mouthfeel. The authors contributed equally to this work.

items.title: DUS (Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability) Descriptor‐Based Multivariate Analysis Reveals Morphological Diversity and Breeding Potential in Gladiolus ( Gladiolus L.) Genotypes
items.journal: New Zealand journal of crop and horticultural science
items.authors: R. Bhardwaj, Puja Sharma, S. Dhiman, Anju Sharma, R. Dogra, Y. C. Gupta
items.abstract: Precise characterisation of genotypes helps identify distinct morphological traits, minimise varietal mixtures and select suitable genotypes for hybridisation. The present study was conducted at Dr. YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni, Solan (H.P.), during 2022–2023, involving morphological characterisation of 14 gladiolus genotypes using 66 distinctness, uniformity and stability (DUS) descriptors standardised by the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority (PPV&FRA). The experiment was conducted in a randomised block design with three replications. A considerable amount of variability was detected for the studied vegetative, floral and corm traits with genotypes showing maximum variation for 21 traits comprising three continuous variables: plant height, corm weight before and after storage which subsequently contributed maximum to variability, that is, 4.24%, 4.23% and 4.35% respectively along dimension 1, and several categorical variables with anther: colour of stomium (6.09%) and outer bract: anthocyanin colouration (5.91%) as key contributors along dimension 2, as confirmed by factor analysis of mixed data (FAMD). The first five dimensions accounted for >60% of the total variation, with dimensions 1 and 2 explaining 17.4% and 13.9%, respectively. Hierarchical Clustering on Principal Components (HCPC) grouped the genotypes into seven clusters, whereas unweighted pair group method with arithmetic mean (UPGMA) generated three major clusters, with considerable similarity in grouping. Genotypes from distinct clusters may serve as potential parents for hybridisation. items.title: Advancing DUS characterization of neem through systematic gap analysis and setting future research priorities
items.authors: Aman Mahajan, A. Rana, J. Jyoti, Yogendra Kumar, Rama Kant, Ashok Kumar
items.abstract: Azadirachta indica A. Juss. (neem) is a multipurpose tree species of agricultural, medicinal, pesticidal and industrial importance. Increasing demand for neem-derived products, particularly neem oil for neem-coated urea, has stimulated genetic improvement programme for development of superior planting material with enhanced production and biochemical traits. In this context, Forest Research Institute (FRI), Dehradun, in collaboration with the Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO), released six elite neem varieties characterized by early flowering and fruiting, with oil content ranging from 35.44 to 43.51% and azadirachtin content from 6047 to 9760 ppm. The development and release of such improved varieties necessitate reliable and standardized distinctness, uniformity and stability (DUS) characterization for their identification, registration and legal protection. However, application of DUS testing in neem is challenging because of its perennial growth habit, extended juvenile phase, phenotypic plasticity and environmental influence on morphological traits. This systematic review synthesizes available information on DUS characterization in neem and critically examines morphological, quantitative, pseudo-qualitative and biochemical descriptors used for varietal identification. It identifies limitations in existing descriptor framework and highlights need for systematic validation across environments and developmental stages. Importantly, review contextualizes neem DUS characterization within recent advances in varietal development and considers its broader utility in breeding, germplasm characterization, conservation, and variety protection. items.title: Integrating Species Distribution Modelling and Spring Low-Temperature Exposure to Assess Climatic Suitability for Actinidia arguta in Europe
items.authors: Athanasios K. Margaritidis, Ioannis Charalampopoulos
items.abstract: Actinidia arguta (kiwiberry) is a cold-hardy perennial fruit crop with increasing cultivation interest outside its native East Asian range. This study assessed its climatic suitability across Europe using an ensemble species distribution modeling (SDM) framework calibrated with occurrence records from East Asia. After occurrence filtering and spatial thinning, 1483 presence records were retained. Twenty-one candidate environmental predictors were screened for multicollinearity and four variables—temperature seasonality (BIO4), maximum temperature of the warmest month (BIO5), precipitation seasonality (BIO15) and precipitation of the warmest quarter (BIO18)—were retained in the final SDM. Five algorithms (GLM, RF, MAXNET, GAM, GBM) were evaluated using environmental cross-validation and models meeting a TSS ≥ 0.60 threshold were combined in a TSS-weighted ensemble. Temperature seasonality showed the highest permutation importance (0.491), followed by precipitation of the warmest quarter (0.316). The European projection identified comparatively high climatic suitability primarily in parts of Central and Southeastern Europe, with approximately 68,226 km2 exceeding a suitability value of 0.50 and 21,634 km2 exceeding 0.60. Environmental clamping affected 10.2% of the European projection domain but only 0.4% of the area with suitability ≥ 0.50 and none of the area with suitability ≥ 0.60. A complementary March-May analysis of climatological minimum temperature showed that spring low-temperature exposure was strongly seasonal. In March, 32.4% and 23.4% of the area with suitability ≥ 0.50 overlapped with Tmin ≤ −1.0 °C and ≤−1.5 °C scenarios respectively, whereas no corresponding overlap occurred in April or May. items.title: Comparative Study of Soil Respiration Characteristics and Influencing Factors of Four Land-Use Types in the Aksu Desert–Oasis Ecotone
items.authors: Jia-Fei Liang, Hai-Lian Liang, Ruo-Xi Li, Lu-Qing Zhou, Wen-Jie Zhou, Fei Chen
items.abstract: Aims: Land-use types and soil salinization in arid desert–oasis ecotones are associated with differences in soil CO2 efflux, yet the combined effects of multiple environmental factors remain poorly understood. This study aims to characterise the seasonal patterns, temperature sensitivity, and major correlates of soil respiration across four typical land-use types, thereby supporting regional carbon budget assessments. Methods: We conducted in situ soil respiration monitoring during the 2024 growing season (April–October) in four representative habitats (Populus euphratica forest, jujube orchard, grassland, and wetland) in the Aksu desert–oasis ecotone, Xinjiang. Concurrent measurements of topsoil (0–20 cm) physicochemical properties and extracellular enzyme activities were taken. Pearson correlation, variation partitioning, and the Van’t Hoff temperature-response model were employed. Results: Soil respiration exhibited a unimodal seasonal pattern peaking in July, with growing-season mean fluxes ranked as grassland > wetland > jujube orchard > Populus euphratica forest. Temperature sensitivity (Q10) followed wetland (3.23) > grassland (2.44) > orchard (2.08) > forest (1.57), a pattern consistent with differences in soil moisture and salinity among the sites. Respiration correlated positively with pH, electrical conductivity, total salt, organic matter, urease, and sucrase, and negatively with available N, P, K, and peroxidase (p < 0.05). Physicochemical properties and enzyme activities jointly explained 70.7% of variation, with total soil salt (12.5%), sucrase (12.2%), and available N (11.1%) as the top contributors. items.title: Sequential optimisation of medium-temperature rehydration and enzymolysis for enhanced juice yield and sugar recovery in jujube juice processing
items.authors: J. Tian, X. Li, Y. Ma, Q. Chen, L. Song, J. Yang
items.abstract: Jujube distilled spirit, a traditional Chinese alcoholic beverage valued for its characteristic aroma and mellow palate, is constrained by low juicing efficiency and high energy consumption during raw-material pre-treatment. This study optimised the rehydration and enzymolysis stages of jujube juice extraction. A jujube-to-water ratio of 1:3 (w/v) and a rehydration temperature of 80 °C were selected on the basis of juice yield, sugar extraction, process compatibility, and energy consumption. Among five commercial pectinase preparations, RVF combined the highest juice yield (84.67 ± 0.11%) with the lowest methanol formation (286.56 ± 0.17 mg L −1 ) and was selected for further optimisation. The enzymolysis conditions were then optimised by response surface methodology, giving an enzyme dosage of 0.35‰ (v/v), a temperature of 58 °C, and a duration of 170 min, with a validated laboratory-scale juice yield of 81.20%. At factory scale, the new process increased juice yield by 17.89% and sugar extraction rate by 20.81% relative to the conventional process and reduced the calculated unit thermal energy consumption by 48.8%. This energy-efficient protocol provides high-quality jujube juice as a fermentation substrate and supports the sustainable industrial production of jujube wine.

items.title: Effects of Wheat Matrix and Jujube Incorporation Form on the Quality and Antioxidant Properties of Whole-Wheat Steamed Bread
items.authors: Rui-Jing He, Jing-Yi Zhang, Meng-Qin Li, Shun-Shun Lin, Dao-Wen Wang, Kun-Pu Zhang
items.abstract: The incorporation form of fruit-derived ingredients may influence the quality and antioxidant responses of whole-wheat steamed bread. Jujube was incorporated into white- and colored-wheat whole-wheat flours either as dry powder or as prehydrated pulp at 5%, 10%, and 15% on a dry-matter basis, while the total water addition was kept constant across all formulations. Product geometry, surface color, texture, cross-sectional appearance, anthocyanin content, and ABTS radical scavenging activity were evaluated. Specific volume showed relatively limited variation across the tested formulations, including a range of 1.59–1.67 mL/g in the white-wheat powder series. Colored-wheat flour contained 4.24 mg/100 g anthocyanins compared with 0.99 mg/100 g in white-wheat flour, and anthocyanin content in steamed bread was governed mainly by wheat matrix. ABTS activity was affected by wheat matrix, jujube form, addition level, and their two-way interactions, reaching 66.15% in colored-wheat steamed bread containing 15% jujube pulp. Among the formulations tested, 10% jujube pulp in the colored-wheat system provided a more balanced response in product shape and antioxidant activity, whereas increasing the level to 15% further enhanced ABTS activity but reduced several instrumental texture attributes.

items.title: Persimmon peel polyphenols modulate the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway to exert prebiotic effects: implications for high-value utilization.
items.authors: Zhou X, Zhang C, Tian B, Zhang B, Zhao H.
items.abstract: Persimmon (Diospyros kaki 'Fuping Jianshi') peel is a by-product of persimmon processing, which is rich in polyphenols. In this study, the ultrasound-assisted ethanol extraction and purification of persimmon peel polyphenols (PPP) were optimized, and the PPP with yielding a final total phenolic content (TPC) of 287.52 ± 4.10 mg GAE/g of 287.52 ± 4.10 mg GAE/g was obtained. Using UPLC-MS/MS, 796 compounds were identified from PPP, which were primarily phenolic acids. PPP significantly promoted the growth of Lactobacillus acidophilus NCFM and exhibited prebiotic activity. In vitro colonic fermentation showed that PPP promoted Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes, inhibited Proteobacteria and Escherichia-Shigella, and significantly increased Short-Chain Fatty Acids (SCFAs) production. Multi-omics analysis elucidated that the biotransformation of PPP is closely associated with a reciprocal feedback loop with gut microbiota, potentially modulated by the specific enrichment of flavonoid biosynthetic pathways. These results indicated that PPP possesses strong antioxidant and gut regulatory properties, supporting its value as a functional food ingredient or nutritional component, and promoting the valorization of persimmon peel.

items.title: GWAS-biologically informed SNP selection improves genomic relationship matrices and genetic parameter estimation in forest trees: insights from spruce and Eucalyptus
items.authors: Y. El-Kassaby, E. P. Cappa
items.abstract: Accurate estimation of quantitative genetic parameters is critical for genomic selection in forest tree breeding. Compared with pedigree-based relationship matrices ( A -matrices), genomic relationship matrices ( G -matrices) better capture realized genetic relationships, including Mendelian sampling and cryptic relatedness. This study evaluated a genome-wide association study (GWAS)-based SNP selection strategy to improve G -matrix construction and estimates of additive genetic variance, heritability, and breeding values in white spruce ( Picea glauca ) and Eucalyptus ( Eucalyptus grandis ), two species with contrasting genome sizes and genotyping platforms. Progeny trials were analyzed using both pedigree-based best linear unbiased prediction (ABLUP) and genomic BLUP (GBLUP). Genomic relationship matrices were constructed from complete SNP datasets and compared with pedigree-based relationship matrices. To evaluate the impact of marker selection, SNPs were ranked according to the absolute magnitude of their GWAS-estimated effects, and sequential subsets of informative markers were used to reconstruct G -matrices. Parameter estimates and theoretical accuracy from reduced SNP panels were compared with those from the complete datasets. Genomic relationship matrices generated connected family networks, revealing hidden relatedness and overcoming limitations of pedigree-based relationships. GBLUP yielded consistently higher heritability estimates for all traits in white spruce but only for tree volume in Eucalyptus. GWAS-informed SNP selection showed that marker informativeness was more important than marker number; in white spruce, ~50,000 informative SNPs performed comparably to the full 467K SNP panel for some traits, although marker requirements varied among traits. items.title: Genetic Diversity Analysis of Quinoa Germplasm Based on Phenotypic Traits and SSR Molecular Markers
items.authors: Y. Lai, Siyi Liu, Xin-Chun Liu, Jin'e Yuan, Xia Xu, Xing-Jin Ma
items.abstract: Quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) stands out as a versatile cereal crop, celebrated for its exceptional nutritional content and medicinal properties, as well as a wide range of morphological and genomic variations. Despite numerous studies on the genetic diversity of quinoa germplasm, a comprehensive assessment remains insufficient. In contrast, research focusing on the DUS traits and molecular variation in the germplasm used in China is relatively limited. We thoroughly examined 170 quinoa accessions, focusing on 30 morphological characterizations based on DUS descriptors (referred to as DUS testing traits) and 23 simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers. The results indicated that all 30 DUS testing traits were polymorphic. In total, we detected 136 allelic variations across the 170 varieties, averaging 4.53 per trait. The average Shannon index (I) was 0.97, with values ranging from 0.09 to 1.67. Diversity was highest at T30 (Time of maturity) and lowest at T6 (Stem: color). Using the UPGMA (unweighted pair-group method with arithmetic means) method, the cultivars were classified into three distinct groups, a categorization further supported by principal component analysis. To streamline field identification and screening, 18 key traits were identified based on principal component scores. Furthermore, the genetic diversity of all materials was analyzed using 23 SSR markers. The analysis revealed an average of 11.185 observed alleles, 3.874 effective alleles, a Nei’s gene diversity index of 0.680, and a Shannon’s information index(I) of 1.547, highlighting the substantial genetic diversity within the population. items.title: Application of Machine Learning to Assess the Effects of Ozone Treatment on Selected Mechanical Properties of Fresh Persimmon Fruit During Storage
items.authors: J. Gorzelany, K. Pentoś, Piotr Kuźniar, M. Zardzewiały
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to assess the effects of gaseous ozone treatment and storage time on selected physicochemical and mechanical properties of ‘Rojo Brillante’ persimmon fruit (Diospyros kaki L.), as well as to develop machine learning models for predicting their mechanical properties. The fruits were exposed to ozone at a concentration of 10 ppm for 15 or 30 min, while the control samples remained untreated. The ozonation treatment was applied once as a pre-treatment on day 0, prior to the start of storage; no further ozone exposure was applied during the subsequent 20-day storage period. The fruits were then stored for 20 days at 3 °C and 80% relative humidity. The analysed parameters included CIE Lab* colour coordinates, chemical and morphological properties, water content, puncture force, deformation, failure energy, and the Fmax/dL ratio. Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Regression, and XGBoost algorithms were used to predict the mechanical properties, and their performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Storage time significantly affected all analysed mechanical properties, resulting in decreases in water content, puncture force, failure energy, and the Fmax/dL ratio, accompanied by an increase in fruit deformation. The 30 min treatment was associated with slightly higher values of selected mechanical parameters; however, the differences among the ozonation variants were limited and did not apply to all of the analysed characteristics. The highest predictive accuracy was obtained for failure force, failure energy, and the Fmax/dL ratio, with correlation coefficients of 0.807, 0.805, and 0.823, respectively. items.title: Inhibitory Effects and Transcriptomic Insights of L-Arginine Against <i>Diaporthe nobilis</i>.
items.authors: Zhou S, Wang X, Wang Z, Duan L, Feng J, Yan DH.
items.abstract: Diaporthe nobilis causes postharvest decay in Chinese chestnuts ( Castanea mollissima Blume). This study evaluated the effects of exogenous L-arginine (L-Arg) on fungal growth, fruit decay, and transcriptional responses using a single D. nobilis isolate. In a preliminary in vitro screen of nine amino acids at 30 mM, L-Arg showed the strongest inhibition of mycelial growth. L-Arg inhibited mycelial growth in a concentration-dependent manner in vitro. In the single fruit assay, the 2.5-20 mM groups had lower observed disease incidence and disease indices than the water control, whereas the 30 mM group had values close to the control. Transcriptomic analysis of mycelia grown on potato dextrose agar (PDA) showed lower transcript levels for several genes annotated as encoding membrane transporters, cell wall-degrading enzymes (CWDEs), and proteins involved in secondary metabolism under L-Arg treatment. These findings describe transcriptional responses under in vitro culture conditions. Without functional or biochemical validation, they do not establish reduced CWDE activity or suppression of virulence during host infection. The contrasting responses of fungal growth and fruit decay indicate that stronger inhibition in vitro does not necessarily translate into better disease control. Further studies across isolates, together with measurements during infection and functional validation, are needed to assess the mechanisms and practical value of L-Arg for postharvest chestnut protection.

items.title: TURLI TUPROQ-IQLIM SHAROITLARIDA DORIVOR O‘SIMLIK MARMARAK (SALVIA L.) NING MORFOLOGIK VA BIOLOGIK XUSUSIYATLARI
items.authors: Suroj Qurbanboyev
items.abstract: The article analyzes the morphological and biological characteristics of the medicinal plant sage (Salvia L.) grown under different soil-climatic conditions. On sierozem, chestnut, and saline soils of lowland, foothill, and mountain zones, plant height, leaf structure, glandular hair density, and tissue thickness were found to vary depending on ecological factors. The content of essential oil, phenolic compounds, and flavonoids was comparatively assessed. The findings help identify optimal agroecological zones for producing raw material with high biological activity.

items.title: Evaluation of Nutritional, Structural and Sensory Properties of Cookies Supplemented with Water Chestnut Flour
items.authors: Aqsa Zulfiqar, Hanzla Attiq
items.abstract: Trapa natans L. is commonly known as “waste chestnut” or “singhara nuts”. It belongs to an aquatic genus native to tropical and temperate regions. It is commercially recognized due to its nutritional composition and edible fruits. Despite being rich in proteins, minerals, lipids, carbohydrates, polyphenols, vitamins, hydrolysable tannins, and dietary fibres, they have not been fully marketed because they have limited availability. The research investigates the potential application of water chestnut flour in cookies, focusing on rheological, physical, mineral, antimicrobial, and sensory characteristics to enhance the flavor of cookies. The study emphasizes notable characteristics of the water chestnut flour, focusing on its impact on the durability and flavor of the cookies. The proximate analysis of water chestnut flour demonstrated results of protein (4.67±1.86%), crude fat (1.98±0.08%), moisture (65.33±0.45%), ash (2.45±0.14%) crude fiber (0.73±0.05%) and nitrogen-free extract (24.84±0.5%). items.title: Magnesium-associated persimmon polysaccharide modulates the structure, water mobility, and texture of kudzu starch gels.
items.authors: Lu L, Shi T, Zhu Y, Li X, Wu C, Zhou D, Li T, Fan G.
items.abstract: This study evaluated how a magnesium-associated persimmon polysaccharide preparation (PP-Mg) affected kudzu starch (KS) gels. Persimmon polysaccharide (PP) and MgCl 2 were combined at mass ratios of 4:1, 4:2, and 4:3. PP-Mg 4:2 had the highest geometric mean apparent viscosity across the shear-rate sweep and the highest viscoelastic moduli within the common strain interval. It also ranked first in a four-criterion comparison. This preparation was then added at 0.8% or 2.0% (w/v) to dispersions containing 15%, 20%, or 25% (w/v) KS before gelatinization. The six gels were compared using utensil tests, texture profile analysis, rheology, water mobility, and deformation stability. The 2.0% PP-Mg/20% KS gel ranked first in the combined evaluation (C i = 0.927). It showed good cohesion during handling, moderate hardness, predominantly elastic behavior, and restricted water mobility. Its mean observational texture score was 93.5/100 across six assessors. This score was developed for this study and is not an official score of the International Dysphagia Diet Standardisation Initiative (IDDSI). The same gel ranked first when the observational texture score was excluded. These results identify 2.0% PP-Mg/20% KS as the preferred formulation among the gels tested under the stated preparation conditions.

items.title: Detection of Eulecanium giganteum Infestation in Jujube Orchards Based on UAV Multispectral Remote Sensing
items.authors: Y. Chao, Yu-Long Wang, Zhuo-Yang Xu, Ruo-Hong He, Rina Yangdao, Hong-Qiang Dong
items.abstract: The application of remote sensing technology to monitor agricultural pests and diseases provides an effective approach for rapid and non-destructive assessment of crop health. This study evaluated a UAV multispectral remote sensing framework integrating vegetation indices and SPAD information for assessing Eulecanium giganteum infestation in jujube orchards. Initially, 24 vegetation indices were extracted from canopy multispectral imagery, and Pearson correlation analysis was used for feature screening, resulting in a refined subset of 19 vegetation indices. Seven machine learning algorithms were evaluated during model development, with Grid Search combined with tree-level grouped 7-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection. Vegetation indices were used as predictor variables, while SPAD value and infestation severity were treated as response variables in the regression and classification tasks, respectively. During internal model development, the CatBoost-19opt model achieved an R2 of 0.81 and an RMSE of 1.84 for SPAD estimation. On the independent test set consisting of 58 jujube trees, the previously selected model achieved an R2 of 0.84 and an RMSE of 1.56. During internal model development, incorporating measured SPAD values improved pest classification performance, with XGBoost-19sopt achieving an OA of 0.89 and a Kappa coefficient of 0.84. On the independent test set, the measured-SPAD configuration achieved an OA of 0.88, whereas both the VI-only and VI combined with predicted-SPAD configurations achieved an OA of 0.71. Thus, incorporating predicted SPAD did not improve overall classification accuracy relative to using vegetation indices alone. items.title: Achieving sustainable desertification control: insights from symbiosis between the Taklamakan Desert-fringe shelter-belt enclosure project and desert-based industries
items.authors: Hua Li
items.abstract: There is an inherent trade-off between ecological restoration goals and the survival needs of inhabitants in desertification control. From an ecological perspective, large-scale planting of trees and grasses, sand fixation through enclosed forest cultivation, and rotational cropping are core measures for curbing shifting sands, restoring soil and water, and building robust ecological barriers to prevent further desertification. From an economic perspective, local residents in desert areas rely heavily on traditional grassland grazing, desert reclamation, and the harvesting of desert shrubs for fuel and forage. This gives rise to the tangible dilemma of “ecological restoration versus subsistence survival” in desertification control. Desert-based industries are considered conducive to addressing the trade-off dilemma between ecological restoration and economic gain. This study was conducted through a multi-case study of the symbiosis between the Taklamakan Desert-fringe Shelter-belt Enclosure Project (TDSEP), a part of China’s Three Norths Shelterbelt Program (TNSP), and six types of desert-based industries embedded in the TDSEP, including the Yutian rose industry, Kunyu jujube industry, Hetian walnut + jujube industry, Shache Eucommia Industry, Shaya centralized photovoltaic industry, and Shaya “saxaul + cistanche deserticola + distributed photovoltaic” industry. It was found that the factors and mechanisms impacting the symbiosis between TDSEP and industry-based industries are categorized into three categories: the symbiotic environment and material factors of production, the technological factors of production, and the transformative agencies enabling symbiosis, thus responding to the research questions proposed in the introduction section. items.title: From Wild-Growing Plants to Promising Candidates for Hemp Variety Development: Morphological and Phytochemical Characterization of Macedonian Cannabis sativa L.
items.authors: V. Stoilkovska Gjorgievska, Ivana Cvetkovikj-Karanfilova, N. Geškovski, A. Trajkovska Matevska, Iskra Davkova Stojanovski, F. Todorov
items.abstract: Background: Wild-growing Cannabis sativa L. represents an underexplored source of hemp-type plant material, but its value for future selection depends on standardized morphological and phytochemical characterization. This study evaluated cultivated Macedonian Cannabis sativa plants of wild-origin (CsW) in comparison with selected commercial cultivars and literature-reported European hemp varieties, based on the assessment of phenotypic differentiation and cannabinoid diversity. Methods: Seeds from five wild-growing plant groups from two N. Macedonian regions, Kočani (W1, W2, W6) and Strumica (W3 and W4), were planted outdoors together with four commercial cultivars with differing cannabinoid composition. items.authors: Tao Yuan, Dong Hu, Meng-Yuan Xu, Ming-Lu Tian, Hai-Long Yu, Lin-Yi Li
items.abstract: To enable the rapid and accurate acquisition of phenotypic parameters during distinctness, uniformity, and stability (DUS) testing of edible mushroom varieties, and to address the low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and insufficient standardization of conventional manual measurement methods, this study used the fruiting bodies of Oudemansiella raphanipes as the research object and proposed an automatic phenotypic parameter extraction method based on deep learning instance segmentation. An instance-segmentation dataset containing 473 O. raphanipes images and 1419 annotated objects was constructed, and the YOLOv11s-seg model was improved by introducing the lightweight feature-extraction network StarNet_s050 to construct the YOLOv11s-star-seg model, thereby improving model inference efficiency and meeting practical application requirements. Under standardized imaging conditions, pileus and stipe regions were obtained from the instance-segmentation results, and image-scale calibration was combined to automatically extract DUS phenotypic parameters, including pileus diameter, pileus context thickness, stipe length, and stipe diameter, while quantitatively describing stipe shape. The experimental results showed that the YOLOv11s-star-seg model performed well in the instance segmentation of O. raphanipes, achieving an mAP50 of 99.1%, an F1 value of 98.9%, and an mIoU of 97.86%; compared with the YOLOv11s-seg model, the number of parameters was reduced by 39% and the inference time was reduced by 27%, thereby achieving model lightweighting while maintaining high segmentation accuracy. items.title: Descriptive Morphogenetic and Physical Analysis of Soils of Various Landscapes (Kostanay Region, Kazakhstan)
items.authors: A. Tokusheva, S. Kuanyshbayev, Z. Bekmyrza, A. Nugmanov, A. Yskak, G. Yermoldina
items.abstract: A comparative descriptive study was conducted to characterize the morphogenetic and physical properties of six soil profiles in the Kostanay region of northern Kazakhstan. This study aimed to differentiate the soil genetic horizons, assess their structural quality, and investigate their physical properties under distinct ecological matrices, including baseline zonal steppes, Amankaragay intra-zonal sandy pine forests, dynamic river floodplains, and agriculturally modified areas. Integrated field macro-morphological profiling and genetic diagnostic techniques were used to evaluate these properties. It was found that the soil cover in the area consists of ordinary chernozem, southern chernozem, dark chestnut soil, alluvial soil, and sandy sod-forest soil. Differences were identified in the thickness of the humus layer, soil structure, and depth of carbonates. The macro-morphological analysis revealed distinct structural and genetic features across the studied landscape matrices. The steppe zone had well-developed, granular-blocky profiles with carbonate effervescence that was depth-dependent (down to 140–150 cm) and localized solonetzic features. The Amankaragay forest sands had in situ weathering (brunic features) and deeply developed humic profiles. The Tobol River floodplain had a complex, stratified sequence with a redox-mottled, buried meadow horizon [A] at a depth of 63–68 cm. The results showed that the studied chernozem soils had favorable agrophysical properties and robust structural integrity. They also had typical humus profiles, which create a fundamental physical baseline for soil moisture retention and provide a foundation for future comprehensive chemical fertility assessments.

items.title: First record of Yellow-throated Sparrow, Gymnoris xanthocollis (Burton, 1838) (Aves, Passeriformes, Passeridae) in Bangladesh
items.authors: A. Chowdhury, Raihan Bablu, Jahir Mahmud Sohag, Najmul Hasan
items.abstract: We provide a new distributional record of the Yellow-throated Sparrow, Gymnoris xanthocollis (Burton, 1838), from south-eastern Bangladesh based on photographs. This is the eastern most record of this species and a new country record. We identified G. xanthocollis based on morphological characteristics, which include fine bills, indistinct eyebrows, grey-brown body colouration with a chestnut shoulder patch, a yellow throat spot, and one distinct, white wing bar. Our new record suggests that continuous monitoring is necessary to better understand species diversity and geographical distribution of the avian fauna in this densely populated tropical region.

items.title: Native Entomophages in the Regulation Cameraria ohridella Deschka & Dimic Populations: Potential and Limitations for Control
items.authors: L. R. Bogoutdinova, Е. М. Савенко, A. Gulevich, E. Baranova
items.abstract: Cameraria ohridella Deschka & Dimić was recorded from Macedonia in the 1980s (Deschka G, Dimić N (1986)). The primary host plant is Aesculus hippocastanum. In Russia, this pest was first discovered in 2003 in Kaliningrad. Since the first introduction of C. ohridella into Europe, many studies have been conducted on C. ohridella parasitoids to identify natural control factors. In this review, we examine the spread of invasive insects identified in recent years, particularly Ohrid horse chestnut leaf miner (Cameraria ohridella Deschka & Dimić), and consider the strategies used by native parasitoids to defeat this phytophage. The review also discusses entomophages that feed on C. ohridella. Studies show that in Europe, C. ohridella is attacked by a diverse range of parasitoids—predominantly native polyphagous Hymenoptera, with the family Eulophidae predominating. The most significant species are M. frontalis, P. saulius, C. trifasciatus, and P. agraules. Significant regional differences in recorded parasitism levels—ranging from 1% to 33.6%—have been identified; these may be attributed not only to biological and ecological factors (such as host developmental stage preferences, as well as spatial, climatic, and phenological conditions) but also to the calculation methodology. The low effectiveness of the C. ohridella parasitoid complex in Europe is largely due to poor developmental synchrony between the parasitoids and their hosts. The composition of the assemblage in urban plantings is also influenced by habitat type and anthropogenic disturbance, particularly the removal of fallen leaves. Finally, we provide an overview of future research prospects, with an emphasis on the influence of parasitoids on C. ohridella population densities.

items.title: Decoding jujube aroma: Integrated extraction, advanced analytical strategies, formation mechanisms, influencing factors, and future perspectives.
items.authors: Gou M, Chen Q, Liu G, Hu X, Bi J.
items.abstract: Jujube is a characteristic fruit of China with distinctive aroma and high nutritional value. This review summarizes advances in the extraction and analysis of free and glycosidically bound volatile organic compounds (VOCs), odor-active compounds, aroma formation mechanisms, and influencing factors. More than 300 VOCs have been identified, including esters, ketones, aldehydes, acids, and pyrazines. Esters, particularly ethyl decanoate, are important contributors to fruity aroma and are formed through alcohol and fatty acid metabolism, followed by acyl-CoA formation and alcohol acyltransferase (AAT)-catalyzed esterification. The lipoxygenase-hydroperoxide lyase-alcohol dehydrogenase pathway and β-oxidation also contribute to precursor supply. Multi-omics and enzymology facilitate the identification of key genes, enzymes, and pathways. Emerging approaches, including stable isotope tracing, molecular docking, machine learning, neuroimaging, and olfactory cell-based biosensors, offer new opportunities to elucidate aroma formation and perception and enable aroma prediction and quality control. This review provides insights into jujube aroma formation and quality improvement.

items.title: Discordant Chloroplast and Nuclear Divergence Among Eight Rubus crataegifolius (Rosaceae) Cultivars
items.authors: Seolah Kim, Yoon-Young Kim, Soon-Ho Kwon
items.abstract: Background: Cultivar identification and the reconstruction of breeding relationships require markers that reflect both parents, yet plastome sequencing is often applied to these problems on its own. Methods: We tested how far chloroplast data alone can go in Rubus crataegifolius Bunge, using one plant of each of eight cultivars from Korean breeding programs. Complete chloroplast genomes (155,664–155,770 bp) were assembled for all eight and compared with nuclear resequencing data from the same plants. Results: The 526 plastome variants were concentrated in non-coding regions, and Ka/Ks ratios well below one indicated strong purifying selection on plastid genes. The eight cultivars carried only five distinct plastome haplotypes: three shared one identical sequence and two another. Mapping to a Rubus idaeus reference recovered 4,872,213 cultivar-polymorphic nuclear SNPs, which separated every cultivar pair, including all four with identical plastomes, and the result was unchanged after stringent filtering of heterozygous calls. Cultivars sharing an identical plastome spanned 27% of the entire range of nuclear distances, and the two measures were only weakly correlated. Conclusions: Plastome sequencing therefore describes maternal lineage rather than cultivar identity among these cultivars; genome-wide nuclear SNPs discriminate them, and the five-SNP panel derived from them is a candidate tool that requires validation on independent plants.

items.title: Leaf Phenotypic Variation in Natural Populations of Chestnuts in Yağlıdere Forests (Giresun, Türkiye)
items.authors: N. Pul, Saim Zeki Bostan
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate phenotypic diversity and population relationships among natural chestnut (Castanea sativa Mill.) populations in the forests of Yağlıdere district (Giresun, Türkiye) based on leaf morphological traits. Leaf samples were collected from 105 seed-propagated trees representing seven populations during the 2020 and 2021 growing seasons. Eleven leaf parameters, including lamina dimensions, petiole length, tooth characteristics, and leaf area, were measured, and several ratio-based traits were calculated. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, analysis of variance, principal component analysis (PCA), and hierarchical cluster analysis were applied to two-year average data. Significant differences were detected among genotypes and populations for most leaf traits. Strong correlations were observed among leaf size-related parameters, whereas marginal traits showed more variable relationships. PCA revealed that the first three components explained more than 80% of the total variation at the genotype level and over 90% at the population level, with leaf size, shape ratios, and tooth characteristics being the main contributors to morphological differentiation. Hierarchical clustering produced grouping patterns consistent with PCA results, clearly discriminating genotypes and populations based on leaf morphology. The findings demonstrate that leaf morphological traits provide a reliable and practical approach for the characterization, conservation, and utilization of chestnut genetic resources.

items.title: Common-garden metabolomics reveals germplasm-associated metabolic diversity and candidate resources for functional food development in dried jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.)

items.abstract: Dried jujube ( Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) is valued for its nutritional and medicinal properties. However, metabolic assessments of jujube germplasm based on materials collected from different geographical regions are often confounded by environmental variation, making it difficult to distinguish germplasm-associated metabolic differences from environmental effects. This study aimed to characterize metabolic diversity among dried jujube germplasm resources under common-garden conditions and identify candidate resources with favorable nutritional and functional metabolite profiles. A total of 66 dried jujube germplasm resources originating from diverse regions of China were cultivated under a common environment and evaluated using LC-MS/MS-based broad-targeted metabolomics. Metabolic profiles were characterized by principal component analysis, uniform manifold approximation and projection, and hierarchical clustering. The accumulation patterns of major nutritional and functional metabolite classes were further compared for comprehensive evaluation of germplasm resources. A total of 460 metabolites were annotated, mainly including organic acids, terpenoids, flavonoids, nucleotides and derivatives, and lipids. Multivariate analyses revealed distinct metabolic profiles among germplasm resources, whereas metabolic clustering did not fully correspond to geographical origin, indicating substantial germplasm-associated variation under common-garden conditions. Organic acids, flavonoids, phenolic acids, triterpenoids, and alkaloids showed relatively large variation among germplasm resources and contributed substantially to differences in metabolic and nutritional profiles. items.title: SMXL neofunctionalization and small RNAs underlie the recent evolution of a plant sex-determining system in Sapindaceae.
items.authors: Zheng J, Mai Y, Sun W, Qin Z, Chen C, Wei W, Song C, Liu X, Su X, Wu F, Wu Q, Yao B, Hao Y, Liu Y, Zeng Z, Meyers BC, Xu J, Charlesworth D, Xia R.
items.abstract: Sexual systems in animals and plants are remarkably diverse. In plants, dioecy often evolved more recently than in well-studied animal systems, making plants especially important for understanding how separate sexes evolved independently from hermaphrodite ancestors. Although various dioecious plant systems have been studied, sex-determining genes have rarely been definitively identified. Here, to investigate flower sex determination in Sapindaceas, we sequenced the genome of Eurycorymbus cavaleriei, the only currently known dioecious species in this family and identified an XY sex-determining system. Integrating population and comparative genetics approaches, we demonstrated that SUN, an SMXL-family paralogue closely related to the Arabidopsis SMXL6/7 repressors of strigolactone signaling, has acquired a neofunctionalized role in flower sex determination in Sapindaceae. In this XY system, we identified a Y-linked non-coding allele, SUN MAO , as the sex-determining factor; it promotes maleness by producing small RNAs that silence the intact X-linked SUN allele. In females, SUN stabilizes the HD-ZIP transcription factor KUN; in turn, KUN activates SUN expression, forming a positive autoregulatory loop that represses anther development and promotes female flower formation. A similar SUN-KUN regulatory relationship is also observed in litchi, a monoecious Sapindaceae species. Notably, KUN is orthologous to the persimmon sex-determining regulator MeGI, a distantly related dioecious plant, highlighting the involvement of conserved genetic elements in the evolution of plant sexual systems. items.title: Metabolic convergence on TOR signaling in the chestnut blight fungus and its regulation by host plant signals.
items.authors: Ko YH, Chun J, Kim G, Yu J, Kim DH.
items.abstract: Transcriptomic analysis of the chestnut blight fungus Cryphonectria parasitica identified 22 core genes regulated by Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1) infection and sectorization. Twelve genes with common phenocopies were analyzed: all mutants displayed restricted colonial growth, intense pigmentation, hyperbranched terminal hyphae with swollen globose cells, and reduced conidiation. Although gene-specific mutant phenotypes existed, responses to most stressors were similar to those of the wild-type. Mutant growth was highly sensitive to nutrient conditions, and growth restriction was notably alleviated by supplementation with 1.0 M sorbitol, nutrient-deficient media, or skim milk. All mutants showed hallmarks consistent with reduced target of rapamycin (TOR) signaling. Trehalose accumulation, a canonical fungal response to TOR inhibition, was observed in mutants via transcriptional upregulation of core trehalose biosynthetic genes, resulting in altered hyphal osmolarity and common mutant cell phenotypes. Plant signals overrode the mutants' phenotypes, strongly promoting their growth and differentiation. Although a severely retarded growth defect was observed in mutants, mutants' virulence remained intact, which can be ascribed to the host-plant signals. Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1)-infected mutants exhibited greater growth restriction, accompanied by genotype-specific CHV1 titers. Despite gene-specific variation, common phenocopies indicate that diverse metabolic pathways converge on the TOR pathway in the fungal response to host-plant and CHV1 infection.

items.title: Comparative Performance of Stearoyl Chloride-Modified Cellulose Sponges from Five Lignocellulosic Wastes for Oil/Water Separation
items.authors: Emrecan Arpaci, Sami Imamoğlu
items.abstract: Increasing industrial activity and oil spills have turned oil pollution into a serious threat to aquatic ecosystems. This study compares five lignocellulosic wastes—rice husk, chestnut shell, tissue dust, cotton lint and chemical pulp—as raw materials for chemically modified cellulose sponges as a sustainable oil-removal solution. Cellulose fibres were converted into three-dimensional porous sponges by freezing and lyophilisation, then rendered hydrophobic and oleophilic by esterification with stearoyl chloride, confirmed by a new ester carbonyl band in the FTIR spectra of all five sample series. After modification, static water contact angles increased from a superhydrophilic 0° to 115–136.5°, and the sponges adsorbed oils and organic solvents at 12–17 times their own dry weight, retaining over 70% of this capacity after ten regeneration cycles. Chemical purity (α-cellulose content and lignin/extractive ratio) was the main determinant of performance: sponges from cotton lint and chemical pulp outperformed those from unprocessed agricultural wastes (rice husk, chestnut shell) in hydrophobicity and sorption capacity, while the latter showed compensating gains in mechanical strength. These findings indicate that lignocellulosic-waste-derived cellulose sponges are an environmentally friendly, high-performance sorbent with strong potential for oil-spill clean-up and oily wastewater treatment, with raw material choice guided by the intended application’s priorities.

items.authors: Ye-Song Ren, An-Kang Lv, Yang Zeng, Dao-Hong Zhu
items.abstract: Dryocosmus kuriphilus, the chestnut gall wasp, is a globally invasive pest that reproduces by thelytokous parthenogenesis. Despite the absence of conventional sexual recombination, the species has spread widely and persists under diverse environmental conditions, but the genomic features associated with this capacity remain poorly understood. Here, a chromosome-level assembly of D. kuriphilus was compared with seven representative insect genomes, with emphasis on repetitive sequences, orthogroups, and gene-duplication patterns. The 2.28-Gb D. kuriphilus genome contained 79.7% repetitive sequences, including 62.3% transposable elements (TEs), most of which occurred in intergenic regions. OrthoFinder assigned 13,271 D. kuriphilus genes to multi-copy orthogroups, representing 61.5% of the protein-coding gene set. Independent MCScanX analysis classified genes into mutually exclusive dispersed, proximal, tandem, and segmental duplication modes, with segmental and dispersed representing the two largest duplicated-gene classes. D. kuriphilus contained substantially more segmental duplicates than the other species examined. Synonymous-substitution distributions revealed low- and high-Ks components representing different levels of synonymous divergence among duplicated genes, and genes in these components showed distinct functional profiles. Numerous local duplications were found near TEs and included genes involved in host recognition, nutrient utilisation, xenobiotic metabolism, and energy production. items.authors: T. Filinska, A. Filinska
items.abstract: Growing global pressures – including climate change, food insecurity, and the imperative for a sustainable bioeconomy – have intensified interest in alternative renewable plant-based raw materials. Trees of the Beech family (Fagaceae), particularly representatives of the genera Quercus (oak), Fagus (beech), and Castanea (chestnut), are widely distributed in temperate regions and produce a substantial annual fruit biomass (acorns, nuts, and chestnuts). Nevertheless, a substantial fraction of this biomass remains uncollected or is exploited inefficiently. Comprehensive research into the chemical composition and biological activity of these fruits reveals new opportunities for their integration into various industrial sectors, in line with zero-waste production principles. This review aims to systematize and evaluate the nutritional and technological potential of Fagaceae fruits, and to identify promising directions for their industrial processing and use. The study is based on an analysis of scientific publications indexed in international databases (Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed) published over the last 25 years concerning the phytochemical profile and technological properties of fruit raw materials of the Fagaceae family. Oak acorns (Quercus) and chestnut fruits (Castanea) are comparable to cereal grains in terms of starch content, while beech nuts (Fagus) are a valuable oilseed raw material due to their high lipid fraction. The feasibility of implementing zero-waste processing approaches within the framework of a circular economy is demonstrated. A concept of integrated fruit processing is proposed, in which the food-oriented pathway focuses on the production of gluten-free flour blends, native starch, oils, and other food products. items.title: Benefits of tannin added to concentrate diets fed to ruminants and monogastric livestock
items.authors: J. Caradus
items.abstract: Additives and supplements are often added to concentrate and conserved feeds for both ruminants and monogastrics to maximise feed efficiency, optimise animal health, bridge nutrient deficiencies, and improve economic returns. This may include incorporating polyphenols, such as tannins, extracted from natural plant by-products (e.g., grape pomace or extracts from wattle, quebracho and chestnut trees) to improve animal performance, biohydrogenation processes, quality and quantity of milk and meat, and to reduce methanogenesis. The focus is solely on the use of tannins as an additive—obtained from either extracts or natural variants of feedstuff containing higher amounts of these compounds —and the use of tannins as an additive directly from forages. A review of 72 studies where extracts of, or plants containing, tannins were added to concentrate or conserved feeds for ruminant animals indicated that 63% of cattle/cow studies and 54% of sheep/goat studies confirmed positive benefits. Reasons why benefits were not observed include using the ‘wrong’ type or concentration of tannin, the negation of tannin effects by other compounds in the extract, an unsuitable combination of tannin type and concentrate, or the developmental status of the ruminant. However, assuming this practice continues, this raises the question of whether tannin expression in the main ingredient of concentrate or conserved, feed such as maize or soybean, would be beneficial. For monogastrics, 20 studies for each poultry and swine were reviewed. The inclusion of tannins in feed for poultry provided little nutritional benefit reduced infection where coccidiosis severity due to microbial infection was measured. items.title: Genome-wide analysis of the GATA gene family in Castanea mollissima reveals key regulators involved in salt stress response
items.authors: Xiang-Yu Wang, Xi-Li Liu, Jun Liu, Le Niu, Huo-Qiang Quan, Tong Zhang
items.abstract: The GATA gene family comprises important transcription factors (TFs) that affect plant ontogeny and abiotic/biotic stress tolerance. Castanea mollissima is a significant economic and food-producing tree species in the Northern Hemisphere, known for its strong wind resistance and soil stabilization capabilities. Nevertheless, existing studies have not explored the characteristics and functions of the GATA family in C. mollissima . The study identified 21 CmGATA genes from the N11–1 reference genome assembly of C. mollissima , which were dispersed among 12 chromosomes. Phylogenetic analysis helped to categorize these genes into four distinct subfamilies, with genes belonging to the same subfamily exhibiting considerable similarities in terms of structural characteristics and conserved motif composition. Collinear analysis further revealed that the major driver of CmGATA gene family expansion was segmental duplication, followed by evolutionary pressure predominantly shaped by purifying selection. Phenotypic indicators, such as antioxidant enzyme activity, exhibited significant alterations, and transcriptomic analysis revealed increasingly more differentially expressed genes (DEGs) as salt stress treatment continued. Notably, transcriptome analysis demonstrated the expression patterns of CmGATA genes under salt stress, and combined with their correlation with phenotype indicators and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), effectively benefiting the exploration of the function of CmGATA genes in C. mollissima salt stress response. Additionally, validation experiments utilizing reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) demonstrated gene expression trends consistent with those obtained from RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analyses. items.title: Sustainable development of multifunctional epoxy composites reinforced with jujube seed particles
items.authors: C. Tamilarasan, Rakan Albarakati, C. Raja, N. B. Karthik Babu
items.abstract: This study investigates the multi-functional performance of epoxy composites reinforced with Indian wild jujube ( Ziziphus mauritiana ) seed particles as a sustainable and low-cost reinforcement. Composites were fabricated by hand layup with particle concentrations of 4, 8, 12, 16, and 20 wt% in an LY-556 epoxy matrix cured with HY-951 at room temperature. Mechanical, tribological, water absorption, and thermal properties were evaluated, and scanning electron microscopy was used to relate performance to morphology and interfacial behaviour. Particle size analysis showed a bimodal distribution with an average hydrodynamic diameter of 1099 nm and a polydispersity index of 0.969. The composite with 12 wt% particles showed the highest tensile strength of 43.5 MPa, which is a 14.5% improvement over pure epoxy at 38.0 MPa. The maximum flexural strength of 148.7 MPa was obtained at 8 wt% with a 7.5% improvement. Water absorption increased with filler content under both conditions, while saltwater absorption remained lower due to ion-retarded diffusion. Erosion resistance improved for all composites, with the lowest erosion rate of 1.59 mg/min at 20 wt% compared to 1.74 mg/min for pure epoxy. The lowest wear rate of 7.560 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/(Nm) was observed at 4 wt%, after which wear increased with filler content. Thermal analysis showed slower degradation and higher char residue above 450 °C with increasing particle content. This study provides one of the first comprehensive evaluations of epoxy composites reinforced solely with jujube seed particles across mechanical, tribological, and thermal domains. items.title: Genome-Wide Identification of the Castanea mollissima MADS-Box Gene Family and Its Potential Roles in Female Flower Development Based on Transcriptomic and Morphological Analyses
items.authors: L. Zeng, Xiao-Yan Hu, Hao Yang, Jia Song, Ru-Xin Guo, Haie Zhang
items.abstract: Castanea mollissima is an important woody food crop in China. Late, sparse, and unstable female flower differentiation constrains the development of the chestnut industry. Here, two more-female cultivars, ‘Longquanzhuang No. 2’ (LQ) and ‘Yanqiu’ (YQ), and the control cultivar ‘Yanshanzaofeng’ (ZF) were sampled at five stages after budbreak (7–35 d) for morphological observation and transcriptome sequencing. Morphological divergence became evident at 21 d after budbreak. Transcriptome analysis identified 2223 differentially expressed genes specific to the LQ–ZF comparison at 21 d and 791 inter-cultivar differentially expressed genes shared across 21–35 d. GO enrichment analysis showed significant enrichment in transcription factor activity and related pathways. Transcription factor prediction identified MADS-box genes as candidates, and 60 MADS-box members were identified in Chinese chestnut. These comprised 29 Type I members and 31 Type II members, with the latter classified into 13 subfamilies. Integrated analysis of gene-expression patterns and predicted protein interactions showed that more Type II genes were differentially expressed in female flowers and that expression patterns differed between the more-female cultivars and the control. The contrasting expression patterns of putative positive and negative CmMADS regulators may be associated with differences in female flower developmental capacity among these cultivars. RT-qPCR analysis of four representative CmMADS genes showed that genes expressed at higher levels in female flowers generally increased during development, consistent with the transcriptome data. items.title: Influence of Fermentation Methods on Jujube Wine Quality: A Volatile Metabolomics-Based Investigation
items.authors: Bin-Bin Li, Qian Mu, Hui-Jing Guo, Wen-Ting Jia, Ya Liu, Xin-Wen Jin
items.abstract: Co-fermentation with Saccharomyces cerevisiae and selected non-Saccharomyces yeasts is an effective approach for producing fruit wines with distinctive aromas. This study aimed to improve the aroma complexity of jujube wine by evaluating multi-strain sequential inoculation strategies. Two indigenous non-Saccharomyces strains, Hanseniaspora uvarum TD74 and Metschnikowia pulcherrima HJ79, were sequentially inoculated for fermentation in combination with S. cerevisiae. The physicochemical properties and volatile compound profiles of jujube wines produced under different inoculation conditions were analyzed using HS-SPME-GC–MS, coupled with electronic nose, electronic tongue, and chemometric analyses. Compared with single-strain fermentation, sequential inoculation with the two non-Saccharomyces yeasts produced significantly more distinct volatile profiles. In particular, the triple-strain sequential inoculation group (MHS) exhibited higher semi-quantitative levels of most ethyl esters, with a more pronounced fruity aroma in the wine, consistent with the results of sensory analysis. These findings demonstrated that the use of multiple non-Saccharomyces yeasts is an effective strategy for enhancing the aromatic diversity and overall sensory quality of jujube wine, offering a theoretical basis for the rational design of optimized starter cultures for industrial jujube wine production.

items.title: Cascading Valorization of Residual Chestnut Biomass: Linking Aqueous Extraction, Reverse Osmosis, Spray Drying, and Solid Reuse
items.authors: Pablo Fernández Santos, Claudia García-Revuelta, Lucía García-Flórez, M. A. González-Arrojo, José Ramón Álvarez Saiz, Susana Luque
items.abstract: Residual chestnut biomass was evaluated in a cascading valorization route combining hot-water extraction, extractant reuse, reverse osmosis (RO), spray drying, and subsequent use of the extracted solid. Two heterogeneous residual Castanea sativa streams were studied at laboratory and pilot scale. Successive extraction at 100 ∘C recovered up to 141 mg gallic acid equivalents (GAE) g−1 dry biomass as Folin-reactive TPC, with 90–93% of the seven-stage response recovered after four fresh-water stages. Reusing the liquid on fresh biomass increased Folin-reactive TPC to 12.0–24.0 mg GAE mL−1. Ultrafiltration did not provide useful fractionation, whereas RO gave >99.9% apparent Folin-reactive TPC retention and 96.5–97.6% total-solids retention; standard batches achieved 86.7–93.5% volume reduction. Carrier-free laboratory spray drying gave a maximum dry-solids collection recovery of approximately 60–62% in the favorable region near 20% feed solids. A representative powder contained 488±27 mg GAE g−1 dry matter, showed a DPPH IC50 of 13.7±1.1μg mL−1, water activity of 0.5850, and a volume-median particle size d50 of 7.42 μm. SEM showed predominantly spherical/sub-spherical particles together with hollow, concave, and partially collapsed particles. Complementary FTIR, MALDI-TOF, SEC-GPC, and qualitative on-flow ESI-MS provided structural and molecular-size fingerprints consistent with chestnut hydrolysable-tannin-related species, while individual assignments remain tentative. After two extraction cycles, residual biomass retained a net calorific value of 18.1–18.2 MJ kg−1 dry basis, although pellet durability decreased. The results define practical trade-offs linking liquid-product recovery and solid-residue valorization in an integrated chestnut-biomass cascade.

items.title: Effects of Different Formulations of Exogenous Nutrient Bag Waste on Soil Properties and Physiological Activities and Root Transcriptomic Responses of Oat
items.authors: Li-Bing Gong, Le Wang, Li-Ping Su, Wei Sa, Quan-Min Dong
items.abstract: This study used typical chestnut soil from Huangyuan County, Qinghai Province as the experimental soil, and selected three oat varieties, “Baiyan 7”, “Qingyan 2”, and “Qinghai 444”, for mixed sowing. A blank control (CK) and five treatments with different ratios of exogenous nutrient bag waste (PF-R-1 to PF-R-5) were established. Through soil physicochemical analysis, microbial biomass determination, RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), the effects of exogenous nutrient bag waste with different ratios soil nutrient availability, microbial activity and root gene expression in oats were systematically evaluated. The results showed that most treatments enhanced soil organic matter, nitrogen content, and microbial activity. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the comparison between PF-R-3 and PF-R-2 treatments exhibited the highest total number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with enrichment in pathways related to ribosomal protein translation, oxidative phosphorylation energy metabolism, and DNA damage repair. These enrichment patterns suggest potential changes in energy metabolism and protein synthesis, although direct functional validation was not performed. Moreover, DEGs uniquely identified in PF-R-3 were significantly enriched in nitrogen metabolism and secondary metabolite biosynthesis pathways; WGCNA identified the coral2 module as the core regulatory module, with its genes predominantly enriched in functions related to transmembrane transport and plant hormone signal transduction, which were highly consistent with efficient root nutrient acquisition and the maintenance of metabolic homeostasis. items.title: Persimmon proanthocyanidins-mucins interaction mechanism: structural characteristics, rheological properties, and molecular docking.
items.journal: The Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
items.authors: Ge Z, Zhang X, Zhao Y, Li X, Liu M, Nie R, Zhao G, Wang X.
items.abstract: Background Mucins (MUCs), as the principal constituents of mucus, are closely associated with the transportation and absorption of various bioactive compounds. This study investigated the structural and rheological characteristics of persimmon proanthocyanidin (PPA)-MUC complexes and the interaction mechanism between PPAs and MUCs to elucidate the influence of MUCs on the digestion behavior of PPAs. Results Atomic force microscopy illustrated that the interaction between PPAs and MUC altered the aggregation state and particle size of MUC. Circular dichroism and X-ray diffraction analyses indicated that PPAs induced changes in the secondary and crystal structures of MUC. Rheological measurements demonstrated that both the storage (G') and loss (G″) moduli of PPA-MUC complexes increased with frequency, suggesting enhanced elastic fluid properties. Isothermal titration calorimetry indicated that the binding of PPAs and their structural monomers to MUC was exothermic (∆G Conclusion Proanthocyanidins and MUC exhibited characteristic intermolecular interactions. These results provide new insights into the development of MUC-based nanocarrier systems to improve the intestinal bioavailability of PPAs. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

items.title: Fine-tuning improves deep learning-based digital phenotyping of lettuce genetic resources
items.authors: Eunju Lee, Yuseok Jeong, H. Bae, Yoon-Jung Lee, Seong-Hoon Kim, Young-Wang Na
items.abstract: Morphological characterization of agricultural genetic resources relies largely on visual assessment by experts, and applying the same criteria repeatedly to large collections is labor-intensive. Image-based deep learning can support this process, but systematic evidence on training strategies suited to genebank trait data remains limited. This study targeted six morphological traits of lettuce genetic resources characterized according to the test guidelines of the International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV). Using genebank images accumulated from 2012 to 2025, six convolutional neural networks were trained with three training strategies under identical conditions, and their performance was compared. Fine-tuning achieved the highest mean macro F1-score in 35 of the 36 backbone–trait combinations and significantly outperformed training from scratch and feature extraction, whereas no single backbone was superior across all traits. Misclassifications were concentrated in morphologically adjacent classes rather than randomly distributed, and for the ordinal traits, errors spanning two or more class levels were rare. These patterns suggest that the remaining classification difficulty was associated in part with the morphological continuity between neighboring classes. The attainable performance also differed among traits, distinguishing traits for which the training strategy alone achieved relatively high performance from those for which it did not. These results provide empirical evidence for selecting training strategies and for determining the role of model-assisted characterization on a trait-by-trait basis in genebanks.

items.title: Distribution, Development, and Function of Resin Canals in Conifers: Insights from Cellular and Genomic Perspectives.
items.authors: Yi Feng, Shu Diao, Xiao-Hui Lin, Cai-Xia Wang, Xiao-Ping Wang, Yang-Dong Wang
items.abstract: Resin canals are tunnel-like tissue structures primarily responsible for synthesizing and secreting resin. They consist of specialized secondary metabolite-synthesizing epithelial cells and supportive subsidiary cells, which are arranged to form distinctive intercellular spaces. In conifers, resin canals can develop during normal development or be induced by environmental stimuli, which often form an interconnected network and play a crucial role in defense against pathogens and insects. Despite their importance in resin secretion and defense, the mechanisms underlying their formation and function remain poorly understood. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the study of resin canals in conifers from the perspectives of cellular development, defense mechanisms, and molecular regulation. We analyze the distribution patterns, subcellular characteristics and formation and developmental processes of resin canals across different conifer species. Based on studies of traumatic resin canals, we propose a developmental model that depicts the initiation from cambial activity to cell differentiation and canal formation. Furthermore, we focus on resin canal-specific genes and analyze the functions and expression patterns of identified related genes. With the advancement of conifer genome sequencing and single-cell technologies, future research on resin canal regulatory mechanisms and functions is facing unprecedented opportunities. We propose a strategic framework aimed at enhancing conifer breeding, particularly for traits such as stress resilience, disease resistance and wood quality.

items.title: Developmental dynamics of ascorbic acid metabolism in wild jujube fruit: an integrated physiological and transcriptomic analysis.
items.authors: Liu S, Li S, Wang J, He K, Gao S, Liu J.
items.abstract: Wild jujube (Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa) fruit is rich in ascorbic acid (AsA), but developmental coordination among AsA accumulation, enzyme activities and candidate-gene expression remains unclear. We compared wild jujube with Ziziphus jujuba Mill. cv. 'Lingwuchangzao' grown in the same orchard across five developmental stages. We measured fruit traits, sugars, acids, AsA, total ascorbic acid (T-AsA), dehydroascorbic acid (DHA) and five AsA-related enzyme activities, and analyzed repeated sampling with linear mixed-effects models. Differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), predicted protein-interaction networks and RT-qPCR were applied to 15 wild-jujube RNA-seq samples; ZjVTC2 was transiently overexpressed in Nicotiana benthamiana. At the young-fruit stage, wild jujube contained 778.75 ± 19.14mg·100g⁻¹ FW AsA and 861.77 ± 17.44mg·100g⁻¹ FW T-AsA. At maturity, AsA content remained higher in wild jujube than in 'Lingwuchangzao' (612.34 ± 13.53 versus 321.22 ± 4.31mg·100g⁻¹ FW). Significant material × developmental-stage interactions occurred for AsA, T-AsA and DHA (P < 0.01). Material differences in DHAR, MDHAR, GalLDH and APX varied by stage, whereas the MIOX interaction was not significant. Transcriptomic and network analyses identified VTC2, GLDH, HXK2, PGMP, and the bHLH gene LOC107430586 as candidates. Transient ZjVTC2 overexpression increased leaf AsA by 72.65% (P < 0.01). Thus, AsA accumulation differed between materials in a stage-dependent manner, and ZjVTC2 was functionally supported, whereas the other candidate genes require validation.

items.title: Comparative Structural, Optical, Morphological and Elemental Characterisation of Jujube-Mediated Silver and Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles
items.authors: H. M. Umar, Jamilatu Sumaila, T. Zangina
items.abstract: Plant extracts offer a practical route for nanoparticle synthesis because naturally occurring compounds can participate in particle formation and remain associated with the resulting material. In this study, jujube extract was used to prepare silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) and zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). Both products were examined using the same set of characterization techniques: X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), ultraviolet-visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). The XRD results clearly differentiated the two materials. The Ag sample showed peaks at approximately 38.27°, 44.45°, 64.55°, and 77.57°, characteristic of face-centered-cubic Ag, while the ZnO sample displayed reflections at 31.91°, 34.55°, 36.38°, 47.60°, 56.78°, and 63.02°, consistent with hexagonal wurtzite ZnO. FTIR spectra from both samples contained bands associated with plant-derived functional groups, along with low-wavenumber features related to their respective inorganic phases. Their optical responses were also distinct. Ag showed the characteristic response of metallic nanoparticles, whereas ZnO exhibited an optical edge at about 392.5 nm, corresponding to approximately 3.16 eV. This value was calculated from the optical-edge wavelength and is not presented as a formal Tauc band gap. SEM images showed rough, uneven, and strongly aggregated surfaces in both samples. EDX further showed strong Ag signals in the silver sample and Zn and O as the main detected elements in the ZnO sample. Overall, the study compares two different nanomaterials produced using the same jujube-based approach and shows how their structural, optical, morphological, and elemental characteristics differ.

items.title: Density Estimation in Heritage Timber Elements Using Resistograph Drilling Resistance
items.authors: Yilién Cabrera Martín, C. Baggio, Silvia Santini, G. Íñiguez-González
items.abstract: Accurate structural diagnosis of timber elements in historic buildings requires minimally invasive and operationally reliable assessment methods compatible with heritage conservation principles. This study aims to estimate timber density in situ directly from Resistograph drilling resistance. To achieve this objective, density estimates derived from Woodpecker impact penetration tests were paired with Resistograph drilling resistance measurements through a mesh to develop a point to point correspondence and calibrate a linear model relating density to drilling resistance and enabling its direct application through Resistograph measurements. The database comprised thirteen historic sweet chestnut (Castanea sativa Mill.) beams from the Cloister of Michelangelo in the Baths of Diocletian complex, Rome, Italy. Statistical analyses included the assessment of multiple window sizes, segmented penetration intervals, model calibration, and Leave-One-Beam-Out (LOBO) cross validation. The resulting model enables density estimation using only Resistograph measurements and demonstrated high predictive accuracy, achieving a coefficient of determination of 92%.
